save_export.title: Save backup
save_export.what: Export save downloads your current game as a .cvsave file. Import save continues that game in an empty slot, or a slot you explicitly choose to replace.
save_export.why: Browser saves stay on this device. Clearing browser data or changing computers can lose them. Export a copy before an update; keep it somewhere safe. The last three local backups help recover a damaged save.

settlement_wire.title: International wire
settlement_wire.what: A bank transfer across borders through a chain of banks. Each one checks it, so it takes days.
settlement_wire.why: Cheap and trusted, but slow: the supplier waits for the money, so your stock arrives later. Order earlier when you pay this way.

letter_of_credit.title: Letter of credit
letter_of_credit.what: Your bank promises the supplier it will pay as soon as the shipping papers are in order.
letter_of_credit.why: The supplier ships sooner because a bank stands behind you. It costs a fee, but protects both sides.

digital_dollars.title: Digital dollars
digital_dollars.what: Tokens that track the dollar and move between exchange accounts in minutes, any day of the week.
digital_dollars.why: Fast payment means stock moves sooner. You need an exchange account, and a new payment rail brings its own risks.

escrow.title: Escrow (pay on delivery)
escrow.what: Your money is locked with a neutral party and released to the supplier only when the goods arrive.
escrow.why: You never pay for goods that don't show up, and the supplier knows the money is there. Useful with a supplier you haven't worked with before.

net_terms.title: Payment terms (Net 0 / Net 30 / Net 60)
net_terms.what: Net 0 means pay now. Net 30 or Net 60 means pay within 30 or 60 days after delivery or invoicing.
net_terms.why: Longer supplier terms delay your cash outflow, but may cost a higher price or require credit. Customer terms delay your receipts: check your cash forecast before accepting.

early_payment.title: Early payment discount
early_payment.what: You give up a few percent of an invoice to be paid now instead of in 60 days.
early_payment.why: It costs a little profit, but can cover payroll or rent when cash is tight.

moq.title: Minimum order (MOQ)
moq.what: The smallest quantity a supplier will sell you in one order.
moq.why: A low minimum lets you test a product cheaply; big orders tie up more cash in stock.

lead_time.title: Lead time
lead_time.what: The days between paying a supplier and the stock reaching your shelf.
lead_time.why: The longer it is, the earlier you must reorder, or you run out and lose sales.

gross_margin.title: Gross margin
gross_margin.what: What's left of a sale after the cost of the goods: price minus unit cost, as a share of the price.
gross_margin.why: Margin pays for rent, wages and ads. A busy shop with a thin margin can still lose money.

cash_vs_profit.title: Cash is not profit
cash_vs_profit.what: Profit is what you earned on paper; cash is what's in the bank today. Unpaid invoices and stock count as profit or assets, not cash.
cash_vs_profit.why: Bills are paid in cash. Plenty of profitable companies still run out of it.

foot_traffic.title: Foot traffic
foot_traffic.what: The number of people passing the shop in an hour. Weekend traffic is higher, but each buyer compares your price with the market.
foot_traffic.why: Visitors are not guaranteed sales. High prices, slow checkout or no staff can leave the weekend unprofitable.

food_waste.title: Waste
food_waste.what: Fresh food you bought but couldn't sell before it spoiled.
food_waste.why: Every binned pastry is money spent for nothing. Order for the day you expect, not the day you hope for.

cafe_rating.title: Rating
cafe_rating.what: The stars customers give your café. They drift toward how each day felt: queues, running out, prices and service.
cafe_rating.why: A higher rating brings more customers every day, for free.

packaging_levy.title: Packaging levy
packaging_levy.what: A charge per parcel padded with plastic, under the Clean Packaging Act (Year 4).
packaging_levy.why: Recycled padding costs a little more but skips the levy, and eco-minded shoppers prefer it.

shipping_index.title: Shipping index
shipping_index.what: How expensive moving goods is compared with a normal year (1.00).
shipping_index.why: When it's high, couriers and imports cost more: raise prices, or buy closer to home.

deposit.title: Deposit
deposit.what: Money the landlord holds against damage or unpaid rent. You get it back when you leave.
deposit.why: It's still cash you can't use while the lease runs.

fitout.title: Fit-out
fitout.what: Turning an empty unit into a working shop: equipment, counter and furniture.
fitout.why: A one-off cost you earn back slowly from sales. Count it before you sign.

payroll.title: Payroll
payroll.what: Paying your staff their wages, every Friday at 17:00 from the company account.
payroll.why: Missing payroll hurts morale fast. Keep at least a week of wages in the bank.

stock_location.title: A second stock location
stock_location.what: Somewhere else you can keep stock, with its own space limit. An order is packed from the place that has the goods.
stock_location.why: Warehouse space costs far less per unit than an office, and more room means bigger orders and fewer sell-outs. But each location's rent is due every month, full or empty.

own_van_shipping.title: Own van or courier?
own_van_shipping.what: Delivering parcels yourself in your own van: you pay fuel per parcel instead of the courier's price, and they arrive the same day.
own_van_shipping.why: It is much cheaper per parcel, but the driving is your time. For a small batch, or when you are busy, a courier can still be the better deal.

fuel_cost.title: Fuel and running costs
fuel_cost.what: The litres you burn follow the kilometres you drive, and wear and tear add a little more on every kilometre.
fuel_cost.why: Every kilometre you don't need to drive comes straight off your costs. A shorter route saves fuel and hours.

vehicle_insurance.title: Vehicle insurance
vehicle_insurance.what: A monthly premium that covers accidents, theft and damage to your van and what is in it.
vehicle_insurance.why: It is due every month whether the van moves or not, so a van that sits idle still costs you money.

delivery_run.title: Delivery runs: pay and deadlines
delivery_run.what: A client posts a job with several stops, a fee and a deadline. On time pays the full fee, late pays less, and a run left undone is cancelled.
delivery_run.why: What you earn is the fee minus fuel, upkeep and your time. Take the runs you can finish before the deadline.

route_planning.title: Route planning
route_planning.what: The order you visit the stops in. The shortest round trip is rarely the order on the client's list.
route_planning.why: A shorter route burns less fuel and takes less time, so the run finishes earlier and pays a little more.

driver_staff.title: Van driver
driver_staff.what: An employee who takes your van out on one posted run each workday and banks the fee. They plan the route less well than you do.
driver_staff.why: It frees your hours for other work, but the weekly wage is due whether or not a run pays. Margins are thin, so it only pays with enough runs on the board.

van_capacity.title: Van capacity
van_capacity.what: How many parcels fit in one trip. The rest wait for the next trip.
van_capacity.why: A fuller van spreads the fixed time of a trip over more parcels, so each parcel costs less to deliver.

rail_reliability.title: Rail reliability
rail_reliability.what: The share of payments on a payment route that landed on time. It moves when something goes wrong on the route, and recovers slowly as payments land.
rail_reliability.why: A fast route that fails one time in ten can cost more than a slow one that never does. Look at the record, not just the speed.

frozen_funds.title: Frozen funds
frozen_funds.what: Money you have paid that is stuck on the way: the operator paused transfers, so it has not reached the supplier and has not come back to you.
frozen_funds.why: It is still yours on paper, but you cannot spend it. Keep enough cash outside any single payment route to run the business while it is stuck.

bridge_loan.title: Bridge loan
bridge_loan.what: A short loan that covers a gap until money you are owed comes in.
bridge_loan.why: The interest costs far less than missing payroll or rent. Repay it as soon as the money arrives.

kyc.title: KYC check (know your customer)
kyc.what: Before a large payment moves, the bank confirms who is paying and who is being paid.
kyc.why: It costs a fee and about a day. Order early, so the delay does not leave your shelves empty.

import_licence.title: Import licence
import_licence.what: A yearly permit from City Hall to bring goods in from abroad for business.
import_licence.why: Without a valid one, imports are blocked. Renew it before it lapses, or your next order cannot go out.

compliance_cost.title: Compliance cost
compliance_cost.what: The steady cost of following the rules: filings, checks and the person who keeps them in order.
compliance_cost.why: It is an operating cost, like rent. Build it into your prices, especially as you grow.

valuation.title: Valuation (what a buyer pays)
valuation.what: A buyer usually pays a multiple of yearly profit, plus the company's cash and stock, minus what it owes.
valuation.why: It shows what your business is worth today, and why both profit and cash matter.

earn_out.title: Earn-out
earn_out.what: Part of the price is paid later, and only if the company keeps hitting agreed targets.
earn_out.why: You can ask for a higher headline price, but you carry the risk after the sale.

purchase_cancel.title: Purchase cancellation
purchase_cancel.what: Cancel a purchase still on the way within the supplier cancellation window (normally 24 hours). The normal fee is 5%; payments that have not cleared return the full principal.
purchase_cancel.why: Fix a wrong order before it arrives. Settlement fees stay paid; an unpaid invoice is reduced instead of returning cash.

purchase_return.title: Supplier returns
purchase_return.what: Local suppliers normally accept stock within 14 days of arrival. You can return only unsold, unreserved units at the original delivery location.
purchase_return.why: Stock leaves now. Pay freight now; the supplier refunds the original purchase price less the restocking fee after receiving it, normally in 3 days.

restocking_fee.title: Restocking fee
restocking_fee.what: The supplier normally deducts 15% of the original purchase value on a return. Aurelia Makers charges no cancellation or restocking fee.
restocking_fee.why: Refunds use the original purchase price. Your books remove stock at its current average cost; the difference is an expense or other income.

contract_closure.title: Contracts after company closure
contract_closure.what: Unanswered offers are withdrawn; undelivered contracts are terminated without an extra penalty. Unpaid delivered invoices are sold to a collector in the liquidation.
contract_closure.why: The existing liquidation pays 80% of receivables once. The closed company cannot collect again or use your new company stock; old contracts remain visible as records.

loan_eligibility.title: Loan eligibility
loan_eligibility.what: Check all six lending conditions before signing. A missed condition shows its gap and where to fix it.
loan_eligibility.why: An appointment gets you to Marcus; it does not waive the company, account, credit, payment history, age or collateral requirements.

accounts_receivable.title: Receivables
accounts_receivable.what: Money customers owe for delivered goods or work; ShopLane also holds sales before payout.
accounts_receivable.why: A $1,000 invoice on Net 30 earns revenue today but cannot pay payroll until the cash arrives.

cash_forecast.title: Cash forecast
cash_forecast.what: An estimate of cash coming in and going out over the next nine weeks. It includes bills and expected sales, but not new stock purchases.
cash_forecast.why: If payroll lands before a customer pays, profitable sales can still leave cash below zero. Order stock only after allowing for that gap.

opex.title: Operating expenses
opex.what: Costs of running the business beyond the stock sold: advertising, shipping, rent, staff and servers.
opex.why: Revenue of $1,000 minus $600 stock cost leaves $400 gross profit; $300 operating expenses leave only $100 business profit.

marketplace_fee.title: Marketplace fee
marketplace_fee.what: ShopLane keeps 10% of each sale before paying you.
marketplace_fee.why: A $20 sale leaves $18 before stock, advertising and shipping. Set prices using the amount you keep.

payout_schedule.title: Weekly payouts
payout_schedule.what: ShopLane holds completed sales in a marketplace balance and transfers them on its weekly payout schedule.
payout_schedule.why: A busy sales day raises receivables before checking cash. Keep enough cash for bills until the payout.

ads_cpc.title: Advertising budget
ads_cpc.what: Your daily ad budget buys product exposure; clicks can cost money without creating an order.
ads_cpc.why: An extra $20 of ads must earn more than $20 of additional margin to help profit. Pause ads when cash is tight.

price_elasticity.title: Price and demand
price_elasticity.what: Demand changes when your price moves relative to the market price. A higher price earns more per sale but can reduce orders.
price_elasticity.why: Compare orders per day and unit margin after a price change; selling twice as many units is not useful if each loses money.

product_photo.title: Product photos
product_photo.what: A listing needs photos. You can spend time shooting them or pay Studio Lumen for professional photos.
product_photo.why: Self photos take 1 hour 20 minutes; studio photos cost $120. Better presentation can help orders, but keep cash for stock.

supplier_terms.title: Supplier credit
supplier_terms.what: Eligible registered companies can buy from some suppliers now and pay after the stated number of days.
supplier_terms.why: Net 30 leaves cash available today but creates a bill in 30 days. Reserve money for that bill in your forecast.

avg_cost.title: Average stock cost
avg_cost.what: The ledger averages what you paid for the units of a product at a stock location.
avg_cost.why: Buy 10 units at $5 and 10 at $7: average cost is $6. This cost determines profit when a unit sells.

defect_rate.title: Defect rate
defect_rate.what: The supplier offer estimates the share of incoming units that may be unusable. The actual receipt can differ.
defect_rate.why: At 5%, a 100-unit order averages about 5 duds. Allow spare stock before promising a large delivery.

morale.title: Staff morale
morale.what: A staff member morale score measures how they feel about work and pay.
morale.why: Late wages hurt morale and can make staff leave. A raise helps, but adds to every weekly payroll.

employer_registration.title: Employer registration
employer_registration.what: Register your company as an employer at City Hall before hiring staff.
employer_registration.why: Registration costs $150. After hiring, reserve cash for wages every Friday at 17:00.

upfront.title: Upfront payment
upfront.what: The buyer pays a percentage of the contract before delivery; the remainder follows the payment terms.
upfront.why: A 30% advance on $1,000 brings $300 now and leaves $700 to collect later. It helps fund stock without increasing total revenue.

late_penalty.title: Late delivery penalty
late_penalty.what: Delivering after a contract deadline reduces the amount the buyer pays by the agreed penalty rate.
late_penalty.why: A 10% penalty on $1,000 costs $100. Check stock and supplier lead time before signing.

mrr.title: Monthly recurring revenue
mrr.what: SaaS MRR is subscribers multiplied by the monthly subscription price. Freelance invoices are separate, non-recurring income.
mrr.why: 100 subscribers at $20 produce $2,000 MRR before churn, servers and staff. MRR is not profit.

churn.title: Subscriber churn
churn.what: The monthly share of subscribers expected to leave your SaaS product. Features and support help them stay.
churn.why: At 5% churn with 100 subscribers, about 5 leave in a month. New signups must replace them before the business grows.

server_costs.title: Server costs
server_costs.what: The SaaS server bill has a monthly base cost plus a cost for each subscriber.
server_costs.why: More subscribers increase revenue and server costs together. Leave room for this bill when pricing subscriptions.

interest_rate.title: Annual interest
interest_rate.what: APR is the annual rate charged on the unpaid loan balance. Credit and the base rate affect your offer.
interest_rate.why: At 12% APR, $1,000 outstanding accrues about $10 interest for a month before principal repayment.

amortization.title: Monthly loan payment
amortization.what: A regular payment covers interest and repays part of the principal until the loan is paid off.
amortization.why: A longer term lowers the monthly burden but can increase total interest. Compare both before borrowing.

credit_history.title: Credit history
credit_history.what: Your credit score and record of repayments affect whether the bank lends and how much it offers.
credit_history.why: Pay bills on time to protect credit; an appointment alone cannot override unpaid arrears or a low score.

overdraft.title: Overdraft
overdraft.what: Cash below zero is money you owe rather than cash available to spend.
overdraft.why: A negative account can trigger warnings and insolvency. Review the forecast and reduce costs before more bills arrive.

company_registration.title: Company registration
company_registration.what: City Hall registers a separate company that can open a bank account, hire staff and sign business contracts.
company_registration.why: Registration does not move personal cash into the company. Open the business account at Nexus Bank and choose founder capital next.

food_licence.title: Food handling licence
food_licence.what: Your cafe needs an inspection and City Hall permission before serving food and drinks.
food_licence.why: Apply after leasing the premises. Processing takes 2 days, so plan fit-out and opening around that wait.

green_grant.title: Green business grant
green_grant.what: From Year 4, registered companies using recycled packaging and selling a green product can apply for a grant.
green_grant.why: The permit screen lists the next missing step. Switching packaging alone is not enough without a green product on sale.

courier_tiers.title: Courier or self delivery
courier_tiers.what: Economy and Express couriers charge money; carrying parcels to PostPoint uses your own time.
courier_tiers.why: Economy takes 3 days and Express 1 day. Compare the quoted batch cost with the time a PostPoint trip takes.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.what: Sales earned for goods or work, before subtracting refunds and costs. Earning revenue does not always mean receiving cash today.
revenue.why: A $1,000 delivered invoice can appear in revenue while its cash is still due in 30 days.

cogs.title: Cost of goods sold
cogs.what: The average book cost of stock sold to customers during the month. Stock still on the shelf is inventory, not this expense.
cogs.why: Sell 10 units with average cost $6: COGS is $60. Subtract it from net revenue to find gross profit.

segments.title: Business segments
segments.what: A segment groups transactions from one industry.
segments.why: Separate results show which business pays for shared office and staff costs.

manufacturing.title: Manufacturing
manufacturing.what: Turn raw materials into OEM orders using paid machine capacity.
manufacturing.why: Deposits are liabilities until delivery. Idle machines still cost rent.

manufacturing_rfq.title: OEM orders
manufacturing_rfq.what: An RFQ specifies units, deadline, price range and maximum defects.
manufacturing_rfq.why: A low quote may lose money; a high quote loses the client.

manufacturing_schedule.title: Machine schedule
manufacturing_schedule.what: Allocate weekly hours. Each machine needs one hour between batches.
manufacturing_schedule.why: Overlapping orders cannot share a machine; overtime costs 1.5 times normal wages.

manufacturing_quality.title: Sampling inspection
manufacturing_quality.what: Inspection slows production and catches defects that need paid rework.
manufacturing_quality.why: Escaped defects trigger refunds, fines and lower credit.

real_estate.title: Real Estate
real_estate.what: Brokerage earns a commission only on a completed client match. Ownership adds mortgage and tenant risks.
real_estate.why: Start with brokerage, then buy a rental, then develop Lot 7.

realty_match.title: Match score
realty_match.what: Budget, rooms, neighborhood and urgency determine client fit. Negotiation changes commission and acceptance.
realty_match.why: A high asking price can fail. Viewings still cost time and money.

mortgage.title: Property mortgage
mortgage.what: Borrow against a specific home with a down payment and a long monthly amortization.
mortgage.why: Variable interest and vacancy can make cash flow negative.

development.title: Ruiz development
development.what: Pay construction milestones on an approved, named project. Delays and overruns change the budget.
development.why: Completion creates saleable or rentable units and a visible building.

media.title: Campaign agency
media.what: Pitch for client Jobs, run a budgeted campaign, then settle actual work.
media.why: A rejected pitch still costs time and money.

media_mix.title: CPM and saturation
media_mix.what: CPM is the cost of one thousand impressions. Repeated spending on one channel produces less fresh reach.
media_mix.why: Distribute spending by audience, not just the cheapest CPM.

creative_pitch.title: Creative quality
creative_pitch.what: Slogan, visual and tone should match the client audience preferences.
creative_pitch.why: Quality changes click-through and KPI results.

media_kpi.title: Campaign KPI
media_kpi.what: A campaign aims for relevant reach or conversions, then reports actual measured results.
media_kpi.why: A missed target lowers reputation and future brief opportunities.

owned_media.title: Owned audience and inventory
owned_media.what: Buy Campus Radio as a depreciating asset and sell finite audience impressions.
owned_media.why: Ad contracts earn money; an unsold audience still costs upkeep.

hotel.title: Hotel revenue management
hotel.what: Rooms are perishable: an empty room tonight earns nothing tomorrow. You choose prices, channels and overbooking; a night audit sells the rooms.
hotel.why: Occupancy times average daily rate (ADR) is room revenue.

hotel_calendar.title: Demand calendar
hotel_calendar.what: Expected demand per day comes from weekday, season and city events such as festivals or trade fairs.
hotel_calendar.why: Raise prices on gold days and be careful before locking group rooms on them.

hotel_adr.title: ADR and RevPAR
hotel_adr.what: ADR is revenue per sold room. RevPAR is revenue per available room, whether sold or not.
hotel_adr.why: A high price with empty rooms can earn less than a lower price that sells out.

hotel_channels.title: Channels and commission
hotel_channels.what: Direct guests pay you with no commission. The OTA takes 15% (standard) or 18% (featured) of each night and pays a weekly statement Net 30. Agency blocks give 25% off.
hotel_channels.why: Use the OTA to fill empty nights, not nights you could sell directly.

hotel_overbook.title: Overbooking
hotel_overbook.what: Some booked guests never arrive. Selling up to 10% more bookings than rooms fills those gaps.
hotel_overbook.why: If everyone arrives, you pay walk compensation and the review suffers.

hotel_housekeeping.title: Housekeeping capacity
hotel_housekeeping.what: Each checkout needs a full clean, each stayover a light one. Rooms nobody cleaned cannot be sold tonight.
hotel_housekeeping.why: Capacity, not demand, can be the real limit on a busy weekend.

hotel_supplies.title: Supplies and breakfast
hotel_supplies.what: Linen, laundry, amenities and breakfast are variable costs for each occupied room-night. Your own cafe kitchen supplies breakfast at wholesale cost.
hotel_supplies.why: Breakfast lifts the service score; the cafe makes it cheaper.

hotel_equipment.title: Room equipment
hotel_equipment.what: Room fit-outs are assets that wear out, need service and can break. Renovation restores condition but takes the rooms off sale.
hotel_equipment.why: Tired rooms lower cleanliness and value scores in every review.

hotel_blocks.title: Group blocks
hotel_blocks.what: A travel agency locks rooms weeks ahead at 25% off and pays 30 days after the stay, with a 20% deposit.
hotel_blocks.why: Reliable volume, but the rooms are gone if demand later spikes.

hotel_ota.title: OTA statements
hotel_ota.what: Voyago invoices your OTA nights each week. The commission is deducted from the receivable and the rest is paid Net 30.
hotel_ota.why: Cash arrives a month after the guests, so keep a buffer.

hotel_reviews.title: Guest reviews
hotel_reviews.what: Score 1 to 5 from cleanliness, service and value for money. Only the last 60 days count. Critic Vera Stone's review weighs five times.
hotel_reviews.why: Rating changes your direct bookings and your OTA ranking.

hotel_growth.title: Growth stages
hotel_growth.what: Aster Inn (12 rooms), then the Brasserie expansion (30 rooms), then a Harbor resort (50 rooms).
hotel_growth.why: Each stage needs occupancy, rating, reviews and staff, not only cash.

energy.title: Solar and charging business
energy.what: Quote rooftop solar for real clients, then build an EV charging network.
energy.why: Installs pay once with a warranty tail; chargers earn per kWh and track EV adoption.

energy_roof.title: Roof Survey
energy_roof.what: Place panels on roof cells. Shade, direction and the load limit change annual kWh and the client's payback.
energy_roof.why: A shorter payback wins more quotes.

energy_subsidy.title: Energy subsidy
energy_subsidy.what: City Hall pays part of a system's price from a yearly quota. You file for the client, pay a fee and wait for a decision.
energy_subsidy.why: Grants lower the client's price but can be rejected, run out or be cut by policy.

energy_charging.title: Charging network
energy_charging.what: Revenue is kWh sold times price, minus grid electricity. Demand follows the city EV adoption rate and falls as your price rises.
energy_charging.why: Price too high and the bays empty; too low and each kWh loses money.

energy_warranty.title: Warranty
energy_warranty.what: Installed systems are covered for a year. A claim costs a share of the price to repair.
energy_warranty.why: Ignoring a claim damages your reputation.

automotive.title: Used cars, rentals and dealership
automotive.what: Win cars at the Wednesday auction, recondition and sell them, run an airport rental fleet, then sign a dealership franchise.
automotive.why: Each stage uses real cars and real customers: stock cars back bank loans, rentals follow airport passengers, and the franchise adds steady sales and service income.

auction.title: Auction and hidden defects
auction.what: Bidders have private ceilings. A paid inspection reveals hidden defects such as flood damage, engine wear or a rolled-back odometer.
auction.why: Winning an uninspected car can mean paying visible-condition prices for a worse car, and a later warranty claim.

fleet_util.title: Fleet utilisation
fleet_util.what: Utilisation is rented car-days divided by available car-days. Airport passengers, season, rates and ratings set the requests.
fleet_util.why: A cheap car sitting idle earns nothing; a high price loses requests. Service skipped means breakdowns and bad reviews.

franchise.title: Franchise deposit and minimum stock
franchise.what: A dealership needs a deposit, a showroom and a minimum number of new cars in stock or on order each month.
franchise.why: Miss the stock minimum twice and the factory ends the franchise and keeps part of the deposit.

transfer_price.title: Transfer price
transfer_price.what: The price one of your businesses charges another for goods or services inside the group.
transfer_price.why: It moves profit between segments, not into the group. The consolidated totals cancel it out, so only real savings versus buying outside count.

side_stories.title: Side stories
side_stories.what: Short business stories you can accept from Opportunities on your phone.
side_stories.why: Your company and its progress unlock opportunities. Complete the steps to earn contacts; unavailable opportunities end without a reward.

fx_rate.title: Exchange rate
fx_rate.what: A quote tells you how many home dollars one foreign unit is worth. Rates move daily with mean reversion.
fx_rate.why: Foreign payouts keep their currency. Check the current rate before converting.

fx_spread.title: Bank spread
fx_spread.what: The bank deducts 1.5% from a foreign payout conversion at the current rate.
fx_spread.why: A favorable quote is not the amount you receive: include the spread when planning cash.

fx_gain_loss.title: Exchange gain and loss
fx_gain_loss.what: Foreign receipts retain their historical home-dollar book value until you convert them.
fx_gain_loss.why: Conversion records the difference as an exchange gain or loss. A refund needing new foreign currency can also realize a difference.

international_shipping.title: International shipping
international_shipping.what: Economy parcels take 7–14 days; express takes 7–10 days. Freight rises with distance and the shipping index.
international_shipping.why: Fast shipping costs more. Overseas parcels cannot use your same-day domestic van.

overseas_storefront.title: Overseas storefront
overseas_storefront.what: After Chapter 13 opens the markets, register a company, open international banking and set local-currency prices in Company OS.
overseas_storefront.why: Regions share your existing stock and packing table. Sales and payouts use foreign currency until conversion.

ddp.title: DDP — seller pays duty
ddp.what: The seller pays destination duty before the parcel leaves. The buyer sees a complete price.
ddp.why: Lower refusal risk, but duty reduces your margin. Set a price that covers it.

ddu.title: DDU — buyer pays on arrival
ddu.what: The buyer pays destination duty when the parcel arrives. You do not prepay it.
ddu.why: Lower upfront cost, but unexpected charges cause more refusals and return freight.

tariff_code.title: Tariff classification
tariff_code.what: Choose electronics, household goods, textiles or general goods according to the actual product.
tariff_code.why: Choosing a lower-rate category does not change the goods: wrong declarations lead to duty correction and a fine.

duty.title: Import duty
duty.what: Destination duty is the declared sale value converted to home dollars, multiplied by the region and product-category rate.
duty.why: DDP pays now; DDU asks the buyer on arrival. Include duty and return risk in your margin.

customs_hold.title: Customs hold
customs_hold.what: A wrong tariff code or unpaid DDP duty stops the parcel before international transit.
customs_hold.why: Correct documents with a reduced fine and extra delay, pay the full correction now, or withdraw the goods. After 7 unresolved days, the parcel is withdrawn automatically; freight is not refunded.

trade_terms.title: Trade terms
trade_terms.what: EXW: buyer collects. FOB: seller loads the vessel. CIF: seller also pays main freight and required insurance, but risk still passes at loading. DDP: seller covers arrival duty and risk until buyer delivery.
trade_terms.why: Who pays and who carries risk are different questions. FOB and CIF apply only to sea transport.

trade_rfq.title: Request for quotation
trade_rfq.what: A time-limited estimate of goods, transport, bank fees and risk. Prices are expressed in local currency; the Deal Sheet compares home-dollar costs.
trade_rfq.why: Compare routes before committing cash. This preview does not place an order; refresh after a quote expires.

fx_risk.title: Exchange risk
fx_risk.what: Foreign receipts change home value when exchange quotes move.
fx_risk.why: Compare the cash you will collect with costs already paid in home currency.

forward_contract.title: Forward contract
forward_contract.what: Lock a sale rate for expected foreign receipts, with a fee and refundable collateral.
forward_contract.why: A hedge can lose when the foreign currency strengthens; it does not guarantee business profit.

invoice_currency.title: Home-currency invoices
invoice_currency.what: Ask the overseas buyer to pay home currency on future distributor contracts.
invoice_currency.why: The buyer takes exchange risk and may decline or offer a lower price.

distributor.title: Distributor
distributor.what: Omar buys a batch at wholesale and owns the customer relationship.
distributor.why: You receive less per unit but avoid managing the final customers.

third_party_logistics.title: Overseas warehouse
third_party_logistics.what: Ship stock overseas first, then pay storage and local fulfilment charges.
third_party_logistics.why: You retain retail customers and margin but fund slow stock and returns.

who_owns_the_customer.title: Who owns the customer
who_owns_the_customer.what: A distributor owns the customers; a warehouse fulfils orders for your customers.
who_owns_the_customer.why: Customer ownership changes both margin and who bears unsold-stock risk.

market_consolidation.title: Market consolidation
market_consolidation.what: Larger groups buy smaller brands and can sustain price cuts for longer.
market_consolidation.why: Choose a position from your actual costs and customers; ownership and operating choices are separate.

niche_vs_scale.title: Niche or scale
niche_vs_scale.what: Niche raises price with quality or a paid brand campaign. Scale lowers price and finances more stock.
niche_vs_scale.why: Niche reaches fewer buyers with less price sensitivity; scale trades margin and cash for volume.

employee_ownership.title: Employee ownership
employee_ownership.what: The board approves a transfer of existing owner shares to employees; no new profit is created.
employee_ownership.why: At least one current employee is required. The equity journal and founder carrying value reflect the transfer.

exit_options.title: Exit options
exit_options.what: Keep operating, sell at the current Chapter 12 valuation, share ownership with employees, or mentor with a contract manager.
exit_options.why: Earlier sales cannot pay again. Closed companies create no sale; a founder can still finish the story.

growth_goals.title: Growth goals and achievements
growth_goals.what: Three optional goals rotate after real progress. Locked achievements show hints; unlocked ones retain a dated receipt.
growth_goals.why: Use existing business records to pick your next step. Setting a goal aside never fabricates a reward.

legacy_archetypes.title: Legacy archetypes
legacy_archetypes.what: Seven weighted formulas summarize real records: business types, people, trade, innovation, city projects, recovery, assets and recorded work.
legacy_archetypes.why: Your main and secondary tendencies describe this saved life, not a score that awards cash.

next_life.title: New Game+
next_life.what: Start the next generation or another life in an empty slot. Keep the prior save and inherit only a limited amount of capital.
next_life.why: The difficulty level lowers starting cash and retail demand. Old businesses and sales never become new-life income.

capital_routes.title: Ownership routes
capital_routes.what: A sale transfers existing shares; a listing issues new equity; staying private retains control. None of these transactions is sales revenue.
capital_routes.why: Compare ownership, capital and ongoing obligations before committing.

ipo_process.title: Public listing
ipo_process.what: Two complete profitable years, annual revenue and a clean compliance year lead to a paid audit, three investor questions and share issuance.
ipo_process.why: Audit fees are lost on failure; public capital creates disclosure and governance obligations.

acquisition_integration.title: Acquire and integrate
acquisition_integration.what: An NPC company purchase is an investment with an eight percent systems fee and fourteen days of staff attrition. NPC earnings are not posted to your books.
acquisition_integration.why: Cash or a normal bank loan funds the purchase; a listed company may need a majority board vote.

home_rent_vs_location.title: Home rent and location
home_rent_vs_location.what: A cheaper home lowers the rent actually paid, but the route to your job and business takes more travel time. Studio 1A holds 200 units; Riverside holds 600.
home_rent_vs_location.why: Choose thirty days of notice or pay one month to leave today. Deposits remain your asset, not income; stock and incoming orders must fit.

personal_asset_costs.title: Personal assets have real costs
personal_asset_costs.what: A home carries a mortgage, management, maintenance and tax. A personal car adds insurance, fuel or charging and parking. Furniture changes appearance only.
personal_asset_costs.why: Ownership does not improve business output. Keep personal cash for these costs. Rent can be unpaid; resale prices move and fees can leave negative equity.

labor_cost_ratio.title: Labour cost ratio
labor_cost_ratio.what: Payroll divided by actual café revenue. Weekly shifts share employees across locations; overtime beyond forty hours costs 1.5 times the hourly wage.
labor_cost_ratio.why: A busy counter can still lose money when staffing costs exceed customer receipts.

seasonal_menu.title: Seasonal menu
seasonal_menu.what: The seasonal drink is offered in June, July, August, December, January and February, with fifteen percent more demand for that item.
seasonal_menu.why: Buy its beans, milk and food ingredients before the season; unsupplied drinks cannot be sold.

health_inspection.title: Health inspection
health_inspection.what: Every sixty to ninety days, waste, stockouts, recent ratings and cleaning determine pass, one-day improvement closure or a fine.
health_inspection.why: Clean daily for fifteen minutes. Preparing improves cleanliness but cannot erase past service problems.

second_location.title: Second location
second_location.what: Pop-up Unit 5 café branch has separate ingredients, fit-out, licence, ratings and daily reports. The company shares suppliers and a weekly staff roster.
second_location.why: Assigning a worker to one counter removes that same shift from the other counter; an empty shift stays closed unless the owner works.

route_contract.title: Route contract
route_contract.what: Complete a fixed number of delivery trips each week for ninety days. Negotiate a per-trip fee; missed external-client trips incur a penalty.
route_contract.why: Fees are earned only after driving. Internal café transfers cancel in company totals and never create external sales.

vehicle_condition.title: Vehicle condition
vehicle_condition.what: Mileage wears a vehicle down. Lower condition raises breakdown probability, delays a trip, reduces its fee and incurs towing and repairs.
vehicle_condition.why: Compare used and new vehicles by purchase price, fuel consumption and condition.

preventive_maintenance.title: Preventive maintenance
preventive_maintenance.what: A paid half-day service blocks that vehicle and restores its condition to ninety.
preventive_maintenance.why: Assign another available vehicle while maintenance is underway; neither drivers nor parcel deliveries can use a busy van.

cost_per_km.title: Cost per kilometre
cost_per_km.what: Compare each vehicle's actual fees, fuel, service, insurance and depreciation per kilometre.
cost_per_km.why: The displayed vehicle margin excludes driver wages and the original expensed van purchase; company profit includes those costs.

popup_store.title: Weekend pop-up
popup_store.what: A temporary weekend shop for stock you already own. Reserve at least a day before Saturday.
popup_store.why: Rent covers two days, but sales need stock and checkout staff. Unsold goods return to their original storage Sunday at 18:00.

channel_margin.title: Channel margin
channel_margin.what: Compare actual revenue after stock cost, card fees, rent, wages and transport with the same sold units using ShopLane fees.
channel_margin.why: The online figure is an estimate, excludes shipping and returns, and does not assume the entire batch will sell.

city_future.title: Civic partnership
city_future.what: Municipal partnerships pay actual supplier invoices from a separate authorized budget. They do not award company revenue.
city_future.why: Supplier delivery can fail. Premium contracts cost more and reduce risk without guaranteeing success.

macro_cycle.title: Market cycle
macro_cycle.what: Seeded interest rates and demand change daily. Scripted eras add their effects to the cycle.
macro_cycle.why: Compare cash buffers and costs before expanding. Shocks expire; prices and wages can rise or fall.

market_competition.title: Market competition
market_competition.what: Rivals adjust prices, quality, advertising and locations each week. Market shares include your business and other city firms.
market_competition.why: Your pricing and quality affect demand. Matching a competing job offer raises payroll; letting staff leave reduces capacity.

market_research.title: Competitor research
market_research.what: Compare real shelf prices, packaging and warranty before setting your price.
market_research.why: A premium brand can charge more. Your reviews and margin matter as much as being cheaper.

networking.title: Business connections
networking.what: A gym class can introduce a buyer, courier or local reporter. Each opportunity has terms you can accept or decline.
networking.why: Connections can lead to real work. Membership and advertising cost money; an introduction never creates automatic income.

tax_filing.title: VAT and income tax
tax_filing.what: VAT is collected within customer prices and paid every two months. Company income tax applies to annual pretax profit after carried losses.
tax_filing.why: Collected tax is owed money, not revenue. Filing yourself uses time and risks a form correction; an accountant charges a fee for accurate filing.

legal_disputes.title: Legal disputes
legal_disputes.what: Settlement, a lawyer letter and court have different costs, delays, recovery chances and client consequences.
legal_disputes.why: Claims settle actual invoices, paid contracts, earned wages or completed IP work. Ignored disputes automatically settle after 14 days; no claim creates a new sale.

company_insurance.title: Company insurance
company_insurance.what: Property, liability and interruption policies collect premiums before losses, wait 7 days and reimburse eligible actual crisis costs.
company_insurance.why: A deductible and policy limit leave real downside. Claims are receivables until paid; fines, ordinary investment and hypothetical lost sales are not insured.

company_brand.title: Company brand
company_brand.what: One score combines reviews, published news, crisis handling, on-time payments and employee treatment.
company_brand.why: Good standing changes recruitment, B2B willingness and loan pricing. Short-lived event effects decay; paying for ads does not buy reputation.

personal_energy.title: Personal energy
personal_energy.what: Movement and hands-on work use energy. Sleep and breaks restore it. Below 30%, timed tasks offer less reaction time; no points are directly deducted.
personal_energy.why: Rest before precise work. You can sleep early when energy is low; work is never permanently blocked.

personal_stress.title: Personal stress
personal_stress.what: Debt, unresolved crises and continuous work raise stress. Sleep, breaks, city events and Harbor Point classes relieve it.
personal_stress.why: At 85%, illness offers a free 480-minute recovery day or an 80 AUD, 90-minute visit. It also expires within 3 days.

personal_relationship.title: Personal relationships
personal_relationship.what: Affinity ranges from 0 to 100. Acquaintance, friend and partner stages unlock three personal requests. Gifts have individual preferences.
personal_relationship.why: Relationships introduce paid work and useful information. They never increase demand, scores or profit by themselves.

accounts_payable.title: Accounts payable
accounts_payable.what: Supplier invoices you owe but have not paid yet.
accounts_payable.why: Buying on terms leaves cash in your bank today, but the invoice still falls due. Reserve enough cash for it.

grid_packing.title: Grid packing and postage
grid_packing.what: Select an item, rotate it if needed, then click a free grid cell. Every item must fit before sealing.
grid_packing.why: Larger boxes cost more in materials and dimensional postage. Fragile goods need padding.

freelance_stages.title: Interview, scope and acceptance
freelance_stages.what: Use the client's brief. Research, financial models, operating processes and brand strategy each need different work.
freelance_stages.why: Your work quality affects acceptance. A session uses real consulting hours; no payment is earned before acceptance.

personal_health.title: Preexisting health coverage
personal_health.what: A policy covers most medical costs only if active before the collision. Unpaid emergency bills remain debts.
personal_health.why: Buy coverage before taking risks. A new policy cannot reimburse an earlier accident; cancelling renewal does not refund the current premium.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.what: Updates stay in the notification center. Go opens the relevant formal screen or city map.
notifications.why: Read when you like. Only unresolved actions appear in the HUD badge.
